findings.title: Stop and interrupted answers have no end state: the sheet spins forever, a linked card reads 'done…' and cannot continue, and replies restored after a reload or a server pull stay 'Thinking…'
findings.snapshot_vs_baseline: Identical on both: ask.jsx, LearnPage.jsx, AdaptiveCanvas.jsx, ChatComposer.jsx and SharedBoardPage.jsx have no diff between 3bc489e and feb4825 (verified with git diff --stat). The doc (§11.1, doc line 576) records Stop as 'aborts the browser request; not reported as an error' but not the stuck spinner.
evidence: packages/web/src/ask.jsx:587 - `if (e.name !== 'AbortError') mirror(`✗ ${e.message}`);`. A Stop adds nothing to the empty reply. Learn sends the whole answer as one chunk at the end (control-plane/src/ask.js:379), so any Stop before completion leaves the reply empty.

packages/web/src/ask.jsx:807-808 - an empty assistant reply always renders `<Loader2 size={14} className="animate-spin text-ink-3" />{m.status || 'Thinking...'}`, with no in-flight check. After Stop, busy is false (ask.jsx:592), but the reply keeps spinning with the last progress stage until New chat or a reload.

packages/web/src/ask.jsx:590 -> packages/web/src/LearnPage.jsx:428 - the finally block sends `exchange?.({ id: replyId, done: true })`, and placeExchange sets `{ ...exchange, status: 'done' }`. AdaptiveCanvas.jsx:253 then renders `${exchange.status}…`, so the linked card literally reads 'done…'.

packages/web/src/AdaptiveCanvas.jsx:228,238 - Continue convo is offered on any card with `exchange.status === 'done'`, including one with no answer. canvas-conversation.js:7-9 rejects an empty seed answer, and the per-card AskPanel keeps thread_id null (ask.jsx:515 `...(canvasSeed && !threadId.current ? { canvas_seed: canvasSeed } : {})`), so every retry fails with a 400.

packages/web/src/LearnPage.jsx:191 - a reload resets only the exchange's own status: `.map(exchange => ({ ...exchange, status: 'done' }))`. Its replies keep status 'thinking' (LearnPage.jsx:437), so AdaptiveCanvas.jsx:256 shows 'Thinking…' forever.

packages/web/src/LearnPage.jsx:518 - `if (Array.isArray(chats)) setExchanges(chats);` loads exchanges from the server copy (a fork, another device, or another editor's save) with no status normalisation at all, so an exchange saved mid-answer shows 'Thinking…' or a stage forever.

packages/web/src/AdaptiveCanvas.jsx:253 - most server stages already end in '...' (learn-research.js:37,49,52,59,62,67), so the card shows e.g. 'Preparing answer...…'. The exception is learn-research.js:65 `Retrieval failed: ${error.message}`, which has no ellipsis.

packages/web/src/SharedBoardPage.jsx:65,80 - shared viewers get the pushed exchanges without normalisation. The owner pushes after every exchanges change (LearnPage.jsx:464,540), so a snapshot pushed mid-answer shows 'Thinking…' or a stage to viewers.

Contrast: the Mothership marks a stopped turn `{ ...t, done: true, stopped: true }` (agent/AgentBar.jsx:321) and shows 'Stopped.' (agent/ResultSheet.jsx:79), covered by e2e/rabbit-hole-check.mjs:1599-1609. The dock has no Stop check in any tracked e2e (grep 'Stop' matches only rabbit-hole-check.mjs).
files_and_callers: packages/web/src/ask.jsx AskPanel.send, render branch :784-809 (dock sheet and Ask in chat via LearnPage.jsx:1197 composer; per-card composer via renderBlockComposer LearnPage.jsx:1197; side-panel Learn chat LearnPage.jsx:1291)
packages/web/src/LearnPage.jsx placeExchange :423-429, replyToExchange :434-441, exchanges load :190-192, server pull :515-519
findings.smallest_change: Client only, no storage-shape or server change. (1) ask.jsx: show the spinner only for the in-flight reply (`busy && i === msgs.length - 1`). Otherwise an empty reply reads 'Stopped.' when the catch at :587 saw AbortError (it sets `stopped: true` on the reply by id) and 'No answer received. Try again.' in every other case. (2) AdaptiveCanvas.jsx:253: show 'No answer received. Try again.' for a done card with no answer, the wording replies already use at :256, and show the stage as sent without the extra '…'. (3) AdaptiveCanvas.jsx:238: offer Continue convo only when exchange.answer is non-empty, as Explain in canvas already requires at :230. (4) One small normaliser (exchange and reply statuses to 'done') applied at LearnPage.jsx:191, LearnPage.jsx:518 and SharedBoardPage.jsx:65.
findings.tests_to_add: New e2e packages/web/e2e/learn-lifecycle-check.mjs on the learn-chat-sheet.mjs pattern (page.route stub, no model calls, session clone). (a) Stub /api/learn/ask to send one progress event and hold. Click Stop. Assert the [data-chat-sheet] has no .animate-spin and shows 'Stopped.'. (b) Repeat through Ask in chat on a seeded card. Assert the card shows 'No answer received. Try again.' and selecting it offers no Continue convo. (c) Seed the chat key with an exchange whose reply is {status:'thinking', answer:''}. Reload. Assert the reply shows 'No answer received. Try again.'. (d) Stub the board GET to return a newer server copy with a 'thinking' exchange and assert it renders as ended. (e) A progress stage renders once, with no doubled ellipsis.

findings.title: A non-JSON error page, or a stream that ends without done/error, fails silently in the Learn chat and grading consumers
findings.snapshot_vs_baseline: ask.jsx and learn-grade.js have no diff since 3bc489e. The baseline adds agent/ask-stream.js (Mothership). It already turns a non-OK reply that is not a stream into an error (ask-stream.js:51, tested in ask-stream.test.mjs, which passes), but the Learn consumers never adopted it.
evidence: packages/web/src/ask.jsx:541 - the only check is `if ((r.headers.get('Content-Type') || '').includes('json')) {`, with no `r.ok` check. An HTML 500 or 1101 page is read as SSE (ask.jsx:551-583), yields no events and leaves the reply empty, which is the permanent spinner of lifecycle-1. The same applies to a stream that closes with no chunk, done or error.

packages/web/src/learn-grade.js:20-41 - same shape: `if ((response.headers.get('Content-Type') || '').includes('json'))`, then a loop that handles only chunk and error. An HTML 500, an empty stream and a progress-then-close stream all resolve with no deltas. ChallengeBody then sets grading:false with no verdict and no error (LearningBlocks.jsx:873, 905).

Reachable: packages/web/dev-worker.js:97-109 calls authorizedBoardApp and apiAsk with no try/catch (the fetch handler at dev-worker.js:33 has no outer try), and apiAsk's D1 writes are unguarded (index.js:1198 `threadId = await seam.newThread(message);`, :1200-1210 thread, seed, history and user-message statements). repositories.js:40-42 documents that 'D1 occasionally throws a transient internal error'. An uncaught throw returns the platform's non-JSON 500.
packages/web/src/agent/ask-stream.js:51 - `if (!response.ok) return onEvent('error', { error: `HTTP ${response.status}` });` is the rule to reuse.
packages/web/src/learn-board-request.js:50 - the whiteboard client already ends a stream that has no result with `throw new Error('The explanation was interrupted. Try again.')`.

Related: learn-slash.js:111 posts through api(), and api.js:74 `const data = await r.json();` turns an HTML error into a JSON SyntaxError notice. That is an explicit error state, but not a readable one.
files_and_callers: packages/web/src/ask.jsx send (dock sheet, Ask in chat cards, Continue convo, side-panel Learn chat, and the non-Learn Agent panels that share AskPanel)
packages/web/src/learn-grade.js gradeAnswer <- LearnPage.jsx:563 gradeCanvasAnswer <- LearningBlocks.jsx:855 ChallengeBody.commit
findings.smallest_change: Commit 1, a behaviour fix. After the JSON check add `if (!r.ok) { mirror(`✗ HTTP ${r.status}`); return; }` to ask.jsx and `if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`)` to learn-grade.js. In both loops, track whether done or error arrived; if the reader ends without either, surface 'The answer was interrupted. Try again.' (the whiteboard's wording). Note the ask.jsx change also applies to the non-Learn Agent panels sharing AskPanel. Commit 2, an optional pure refactor: replace the inline loops at ask.jsx:551-583 and learn-grade.js:24-41 with streamAsk, which already frames, filters and errors the same way (the shared rule is in lifecycle-3).
findings.tests_to_add: Add packages/web/src/learn-grade.test.mjs with fetch stubbed as in ask-stream.test.mjs. An HTML 500 rejects with 'HTTP 500'. An empty stream and a progress-only stream reject as interrupted. chunk+done resolves and delivers the deltas. In e2e learn-lifecycle-check.mjs, route.fulfill({status:500, contentType:'text/html', body:'<html>'}) for /api/learn/ask and assert the sheet shows '✗ HTTP 500' with no spinner.

findings.title: Mothership: a stream that closes without done or error leaves the turn open forever, with a spinner (or no end state) and History and New chat disabled
findings.snapshot_vs_baseline: agent/ask-stream.js, AgentBar.jsx and ResultSheet.jsx do not exist at 3bc489e. They arrived with the smart-home integration.
evidence: packages/web/src/agent/ask-stream.js:56-57 - `if (done) return;`. The reader ending is not treated as an event.

packages/web/src/agent/AgentBar.jsx:306-330 - only an 'error' event or a thrown error sets `failed`; bar.js:48-49 set done only on 'error' or 'done'. A quiet return leaves the turn with done undefined.

packages/web/src/agent/ResultSheet.jsx:65 - `{t.text ? : !t.done && {t.stage || 'Thinking…'}}`. :101 `const busy = turns.some((t) => t.kind === 'answer' && !t.done);` disables History and New chat (:122-123) for that scope until a reload, even when some text arrived.
Routing: agent/scope.js:19-22 sends project and canvas scopes to /api/learn/ask (workspace and app to /api/ask, which is off on the preview, flags.js:16).
files_and_callers: packages/web/src/agent/ask-stream.js streamAsk <- AgentBar.jsx ask (project scope asks to /api/learn/ask -> repositoryAsk; canvas scope to the canvas seam; workspace and app asks are off on the preview, flags.js:16)
findings.smallest_change: In ask-stream.js, record whether done or error was seen. When the reader ends without either, call `onEvent('error', { error: 'The answer was interrupted. Try again.' })`. AgentBar then shows the error with Retry and keeps the draft (AgentBar.jsx:327-330). This is the one shared fix that lifecycle-2's refactor reuses.
findings.tests_to_add: In ask-stream.test.mjs, a stream that closes after a progress event, and an empty stream, each end with an error event. In rabbit-hole-check.mjs (bar-page), a stubbed stream that closes early shows the error with Retry and leaves History and New chat enabled.

findings.title: Stop, client timeouts and navigation never reach server model or tool work; the loop stops only if the platform cancels the response stream, and a reason-less cancel crashes the error handler
findings.snapshot_vs_baseline: Unchanged. ask.js, learn-research.js and learn-artifact.js have no diff, and learn-board.js changed only authorizedBoardApp. apiAsk gained the seam parameter but still passes no signal (baseline index.js:1227; snapshot index.js:1219).
evidence: packages/web/src/ask.jsx:890 - `dock={dock} onStop={dock ? () => answerFlight.current?.abort() : undefined}`. Stop aborts only the browser fetch (ask.jsx:532,538 `signal: flight.signal`).

packages/control-plane/src/index.js:1227-1229 and repositories.js:237-239 - askStream is called without req.signal. A grep for 'signal' in control-plane/src and dev-worker.js finds only AbortSignal.timeout on tool, bridge, image, video and math fetches, plus Jev (learn-grade-jev.js:142); no req.signal anywhere.
packages/control-plane/src/ask.js:309-319 - the Anthropic fetch has no signal. planModel's OpenAI fetch (ask.js:264-268) has none either.

packages/control-plane/src/ask.js:364-461 - the answer runs in a floating `(async () => { ... })()` that writes to a TransformStream. It is not registered with ctx.waitUntil and has no cancel handling. index.js:344-346 and :364-366 record that platform limits already killed un-held model work in this codebase.
packages/control-plane/src/learn-research.js:16-22 - `for (let step = 0; step <= 8; step++)` never checks for cancellation. It only awaits onProgress writes (lines 37, 49, 52, 59, 62, 65, 67).

Verifier probe (read-only script in %TEMP%\lc-verify importing ask.js, global fetch stubbed): cancelling the reader after the first progress event gave {calls:2, finished:2, withSignal:1 (the arXiv tool fetch only), onDone:'not called'}. In-flight model and tool calls complete, the loop dies at its next write, and the answer is discarded while the user message stays stored (index.js:1209-1210; repositories.js:236).

New from the probe: `reader.cancel()` with no reason makes the next write reject with undefined, and ask.js:457 `await send('error', { error: e.message }).catch(() => {});` then throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'message')` inside the catch, which escapes the floating IIFE as an unhandled rejection. With a reason (cancel(new Error(...))) it does not. Which reason Workers passes on client disconnect is unverified.

packages/control-plane/src/learn-board.js:343-353 - the whiteboard stream's `cancel() { cancelled = true; }` only stops emits. generateBoardPlan keeps making every model call, so the 120 s client timeout (learn-board-request.js:25) never stops server work.
packages/control-plane/src/learn-artifact.js:51 - artifact model calls get no signal, and the client api() POST cannot be aborted (api.js:68).
Not verified: whether Cloudflare cancels the response stream, or the whole invocation, when the browser disconnects. wrangler configs set compatibility_date 2026-08-01 and no compatibility_flags.
findings.smallest_change: After the reproduction, change the server only. In askStream, create one AbortController that aborts when the stream is cancelled (`writer.closed.catch(() => stop.abort())`). Pass its signal into researchAnswer, which checks `signal.aborted` before each step, and into the model call: anthropic() and planModel take an optional signal and hand it to fetch, and subscriptionTransport combines it with its 180 s timeout via AbortSignal.any. In boardFetch, abort the same way from the ReadableStream's cancel(). Make ask.js:457 read `e?.message` so a reason-less cancel cannot throw from the catch. Tool fetches keep their own 8-20 s timeouts. No request or event contract changes, and a stopped answer is still not stored, as today.
findings.tests_to_add: Add packages/control-plane/test/ask-stream-cancel.test.js from the probe. Cancel the SSE reader after the first progress event and assert the in-flight model fetch received a signal that is now aborted, no further model or tool calls happen, onDone is not called, and no unhandledRejection fires when cancel() has no reason. researchAnswer with a pre-aborted signal makes no model call. boardFetch's cancel aborts the signal passed to generate. Platform reproduction is gated on deploy/model approval: on the session clone, ask a retrieval question on a canvas, press Stop after 'Finding papers...', then read that canvaschat thread in LEARN_DB. An assistant row means the loop finished after the disconnect; only the user row means it died at the next write. Pointing SUBSCRIPTION_ONLY's bridge (subscription-transport.js:4-6) at an HTTPS stub avoids real model calls.

findings.title: No deadline on Learn model calls or on the slash, grading and Continue convo requests, and only the dock has Stop
findings.snapshot_vs_baseline: Same on both. Doc §9 'no request timeout' is accurate.
evidence: packages/control-plane/src/ask.js:309-319 and :264-268 - the model fetches carry no timeout. A Learn chat turn can make 9 sequential unbounded model calls (learn-research.js:16-20).

Bounded calls: tools (arxiv.js:41, learn-wiki.js:67, learn-youtube.js:88 and learn-captions.js:76,88 at 20 s; learn-search.js:85 at 8 s; pexels.js:10 at 10 s), the subscription bridge (subscription-transport.js:6, 180 s), whiteboard client steps (learn-board-request.js:25, 120 s, up to 3 steps) and image generation (dev-worker.js:76, 120 s). Workers AI and Vectorize calls have none (learn-moment-index.js:96,208,246).

packages/web/src/LearnSlash.jsx:37 shows 'Working on /x…', and :80 `{!busy && <button type="button" aria-label="Dismiss" ...` hides Dismiss while busy. The request is api() with no timeout (learn-slash.js:111 -> api.js:68). While it hangs, every further slash command is swallowed (lifecycle-6).
packages/web/src/learn-grade.js:15-19 - the grading fetch has no signal, so the block shows 'Reading your answer…' (LearningBlocks.jsx:908) until the provider returns.

packages/web/src/ask.jsx:890 gives onStop only to the dock, and ChatComposer.jsx:36 `{busy && onStop ? (` shows Stop only when onStop is set. The Continue convo composer (LearnPage.jsx:1197 renderBlockComposer, no `dock`) and the side-panel 'Learn Agent' AskPanel (LearnPage.jsx:1291, no `dock`) therefore have only a spinner.
files_and_callers: packages/web/src/LearnSlash.jsx, learn-grade.js, ask.jsx (per-card composer and side-panel Learn chat), learn-board-request.js
findings.smallest_change: Nothing until the decision below. If approved, add named per-task deadlines to the shared limits module (lifecycle-13). Apply them with AbortSignal.timeout at the model boundary, using the signal plumbing from lifecycle-4, and on the client fetches for artifact, grading and Continue convo, so a timeout ends as an explicit error. Optionally give LearnSlash a Stop/Dismiss while busy, using the dock's AbortController pattern.
findings.decision_question: Learn model calls and Learn client requests have no deadline; only tool fetches, the subscription bridge and whiteboard steps do. Do you want explicit deadlines, and if so, what values: a whole Learn chat turn (up to 9 model calls), one artifact request, one grading request? Should Continue convo, the side-panel Learn chat, grading and slash commands also get a Stop/Dismiss like the dock, or only the timeout?
findings.tests_to_add: Unit: askStream/researchAnswer with a callModel that never resolves and a short injected deadline must end with an error event, not hang. e2e: stub /api/learn/artifact to never answer; assert the slash notice ends in an error after the deadline and the composer then runs the next command.

findings.title: A second slash command while one runs is swallowed with no message, and a clarification then overwrites what was typed
findings.snapshot_vs_baseline: LearnSlash.jsx, learn-slash.js, ask.jsx and ChatComposer.jsx are identical at 3bc489e. Doc §4.4 (doc line 299) says 'silently dropped': that is right for execution but wrong for the text, which is kept unless a clarification arrives.
evidence: packages/web/src/LearnSlash.jsx:63 - `intercept: raw => { if (busy) return true; exec(raw); return true; },`

packages/web/src/ask.jsx:439 - `if (slash && raw.trim().startsWith('/') && slashRef.current?.intercept(raw)) return;` returns before `setInput('')` (ask.jsx:458). The typed text stays, nothing runs, and nothing says why.

packages/web/src/LearnSlash.jsx:21 `const sections = busy ? null : pickerSections(input, { catalog });` and :50 `if (!items.length) return;` - while busy the picker is hidden and Enter falls through to the form submit. ChatComposer.jsx:24 `const submit = () => { if (!busy && !disabled && value.trim()) onSubmit(value); };` sees only the chat busy flag (ask.jsx:889 passes AskPanel's busy), so Send stays enabled.

packages/web/src/LearnSlash.jsx:36 `setInput(''); setProposal(null); setBusy(true);`, then :44 `if (out.keep) setInput(out.keep);`. learn-slash.js:115 returns keep '/<name> ' for every clarification, which replaces any command typed during the wait. :42 `setInput('/')` does the same for the catalog, but that path needs no network, so there is no window in practice.
The window is real: only artifact commands await the network (learn-slash.js:111 `await post('/api/learn/artifact', ...)`), and that request has no timeout (lifecycle-5).
files_and_callers: packages/web/src/LearnSlash.jsx intercept/exec <- ask.jsx send (dock only; the slash prop is set at LearnPage.jsx:1197)
findings.smallest_change: LearnSlash.jsx only, with no queueing. Remember the running command's name. When intercept is called while busy, still return true (the input stays) and change the busy notice to say so, e.g. 'Still working on /quiz. Your next command is kept; press Enter when this finishes.' In exec, restore keep or '/' only when the composer is empty: `setInput(current => current.trim() ? current : out.keep)`.
findings.tests_to_add: e2e (learn-lifecycle-check.mjs): route /api/learn/artifact to wait 2 s, then return {result:'clarification', question:'Which curve?'}. Send '/quiz', type '/graph sigmoid' and press Enter while it is busy. Assert the composer still reads '/graph sigmoid' and the slash result shows the still-working message. After the clarification lands, assert the composer still reads '/graph sigmoid', not '/quiz '.

findings.title: Grading: a late verdict from an earlier attempt lands in the next attempt, a reload mid-grade shows 'Reading your answer…' forever, and an error after a streamed verdict replaces it
findings.snapshot_vs_baseline: LearningBlocks.jsx, learn-grade.js and AdaptiveCanvas.jsx are identical at 3bc489e. This covers client state handling only; the grading contract belongs to C6.
evidence: packages/web/src/LearningBlocks.jsx:848-849,869-871 - `latest.current = block` on every render, and deltas write into whatever block is current: `change({ ...current, verdict: (current.verdict || '') + delta, grading: true });`. Nothing compares attempts, although each commit gets `attemptId: crypto.randomUUID()` (:863).

packages/web/src/LearningBlocks.jsx:881 - `const retry = () => { inFlight.current = false; setDraft(block.answer || ''); onChange({ ...block, answer: null, attemptId: null, verdict: '', grading: false }); };` resets the block but cannot cancel the grade, because learn-grade.js:15-19 has no signal. The old stream then writes onto the reset block and, after a second Commit, appends into the new attempt's verdict. :884 `(block.verdict || '').match(/VERDICT:\s*(good|partial)/i)` takes the first token, so the older grade can tint the new answer.

packages/web/src/LearningBlocks.jsx:863,905,908 - `grading: true` is saved with the block (AdaptiveCanvas.jsx:1147-1150 saves blocks after 400 ms and pushes shared boards via onSave), and AdaptiveCanvas.jsx:1104 restores blocks as stored. A reload mid-grade therefore shows 'Reading your answer…' forever, until the learner presses Answer again.

packages/web/src/learn-grade.js:39 `else if (type === 'error') throw new Error(payload.error);` can fire after chunks, e.g. when onDone's store fails after the chunk (control-plane/src/ask.js:379,454-457). LearningBlocks.jsx:875 then replaces the verdict that already streamed with 'Could not reach the tutor: …'.
The Jev shadow is unaffected: gradeCanvasAnswer keeps its own text and verdict (LearnPage.jsx:566-578).
findings.smallest_change: ChallengeBody only; the grading request, prompts, verdict parsing and Jev are unchanged. Guard every write of an attempt with `latest.current.attemptId === committed.attemptId` and skip deltas and the closing write otherwise. Show a saved `grading: true` with no request running in this mount as 'Grading was interrupted. Answer again to retry.' In the catch, keep a verdict that already streamed and show the error under it instead of replacing it.
findings.tests_to_add: e2e: stub /api/learn/ask so the first grade streams 'VERDICT: good …' after 3 s and the second answers 'VERDICT: partial …' at once. Commit, press Answer again, Commit again, wait 4 s. Assert the verdict contains only the second response and [data-answer] has data-grade='partial'. Reload while a grade is held and assert 'Reading your answer…' is gone.

findings.snapshot_vs_baseline: Same at 3bc489e: renderBlockComposer, ask.jsx and apiAsk's tool list are unchanged. The seam changed only where canvas threads are stored.
evidence: packages/web/src/LearnPage.jsx:1197 - renderBlockComposer mounts `<AskPanel compact composerOnly canvasSeed={{ question: exchange.question, answer: exchange.answer }} onExchange={onExchange} scope={{ app: app.name }} ... conversation="learn" .../>` with no boardContext and no onGraph.
packages/web/src/ask.jsx:569-571 - `boardContext?.onShowPaper?.(d)`, `boardContext?.onShowWiki?.(d)` and `boardContext?.onShowVideo?.(d)` do nothing without a boardContext.

packages/control-plane/src/index.js:982 - every Learn ask offers `SHOW_WIKIPEDIA_TOOL, FIND_VIDEO_MOMENTS_TOOL, SHOW_VIDEO_TOOL`; outline only with body.outline, which this composer never sends. learn-research.js:19 offers show_paper once a paper is read, and repositories.js:239 offers SHOW_VIDEO_TOOL.

Tool results tell the model the card is visible: index.js:1000 `note: 'The learner now sees it playing. Say what to watch for.'`, index.js:1005, learn-research.js:60 `note: 'The learner now sees this page. Say what to look at.'`, repositories.js:198.
packages/control-plane/src/ask.js:404-405 - a shown video still writes a learn_moments row (via env.DB) before the dropped video event.
packages/web/src/learn-grade.js:38-39 - grading handles only chunk and error, so it drops the same events. C6 removes research tools from grading.
Mothership (project asks): 'paper' falls to `default: return answer;` (agent/bar.js:50), and video and papers become source pills (bar.js:45,47). This mismatch is milder: a link does appear.
files_and_callers: packages/control-plane/src/index.js apiAsk research tools; repositories.js repositoryAsk; learn-research.js
findings.smallest_change: Needs the decision below first. Option A, client only: give the per-card composer a handlers-only context. That is onShowPaper, onShowWiki and onShowVideo from LearnPage, plus no-op pause, setAnswering and removeImage and `snapshot: () => null`, because ask.jsx:450, 470 and 493 call them without optional chaining on the method. Replies then place the card as the dock does (note addWiki/addPaper/addVideo also set the dock's next-question context), and still send no outline or attached sources. Option B: stop offering show_* tools on surfaces that cannot render them. That needs the request to name its surface, a new request field.
findings.decision_question: A Continue convo reply can call show_video, show_paper or show_wikipedia, but that composer has no handler: no card appears, yet the reply tells the learner to look at it (and show_video logs a moment). Should replies (A) put the card on the canvas as the dock does (client only), or (B) not be offered those tools, which needs a new request field naming the surface (a contract change)?
findings.tests_to_add: e2e: open Continue convo on a card and stub /api/learn/ask to emit a video event, then done. Under A, assert a YouTube card appears. Under B, a learn-chat.test.js harness test asserts the reply request's research.tools omit SHOW_VIDEO_TOOL, SHOW_WIKIPEDIA_TOOL and show_paper.

findings.title: An outline proposal from the dock lands in the right panel, which is closed by default and not mounted at all on narrow screens
findings.snapshot_vs_baseline: LearnPage.jsx and ResizableSidePanel.jsx are unchanged since 3bc489e. The doc §6.2 (doc line 377) says 'Apply / Discard proposal in the right panel' without noting the panel is closed.
evidence: packages/web/src/LearnPage.jsx:750 - `onOutlineProposal: ops => setProposal(ops),` never opens the panel.
packages/web/src/LearnPage.jsx:90 - `const [panelOpen, setPanelOpen] = useState(false);`, with the comment at :88-89 'The right panel starts closed'.
packages/web/src/LearnPage.jsx:1230 - `<ResizableSidePanel ... collapsed={!panelOpen} ...>` wraps the proposal UI at :1247-1261.

(repositories.js:198); LEARN_RESEARCH_SYSTEM asks for show_paper 'so the learner is looking at it'; LEARN_SYSTEM refers to 'Explain on canvas' (learn-context.js:4-6, :15-16) - none exist on the Map or Overview.

Specs disagree with the code: docs/features/rabbit-hole-t02-spec.md:373 says repository asks go to 'the code-tool handler, which has no research tools'; agent/slash.js:83-84 says research 'elsewhere ... reaches the live model', although canvas and project asks call the same dev-worker model path.

Not every bar send is a model call: exact Map fixture prompts are answered locally (AgentBar.jsx:289-295) and help or Rabbit Hole concept questions get built-in answers (agent/router.js:76-78). Stop aborts only the browser read (AgentBar.jsx:407 onStop), as in Learn.
